A large fluid collection superior to the spleen was also noted (Figure 1).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old postpartum woman presented with fever, abdominal pain, cramping, nausea, vomiting, and profuse diarrhea with foul-smelling discharge, initially suggesting infectious colitis. Physical exam confirmed abdominal tenderness with mild guarding. Abdominal/pelvic CT showed an enlarged post-gravid uterus with intrauterine air, diffuse large bowel wall thickening consistent with infectious colitis, and a fluid collection near the spleen. Lab tests revealed systemic inflammation with elevated bands and platelets, and decreased hemoglobin and electrolytes. Blood cultures remained negative, likely due to antibiotics. Surgical exploration on day 8 revealed diffuse fibrinous peritonitis without any obvious perforation of abdominal viscera. Postoperative repeat CT showed decreased fluid collections, supporting treatment response. No evidence of bowel perforation was identified radiographically or surgically.
